title: Sync report
description: One replication round, as `wipctl sync --json` emits it: what was fetched, what reconciled, whether the trunk was pushed, and every conflict a person still has to decide. A conflict stops the push; the report names both sides so the decision can be made without re-deriving either.

fetched.description: Commits fetched from the remote's plan trunk. Zero when the remote had not advanced.

reconciled.description: Disjoint changes combined semantically — captures, and transitions of different entries. Textual merging is never performed.

pushed.description: Whether the fast-forward push happened. False when a conflict stopped it, or when the push was rejected because another replica advanced meanwhile.

conflicts.description: The facts a machine cannot decide, one object each, empty when the round was clean.

id.description: The entry both sides speak about.

kind.description: transition: the same entry transitioned on both sides, decided by `wipctl resolve`. id: two captures minted the same slug, recovered by rephrasing one title and re-capturing it.

here.description: This machine's side of the conflict.

remote.description: The remote's side of the conflict.

fact.description: One side of the disagreement, in the same words the terminal report prints — a transition with its instant and outcome, or the claimed path. Prose for a person; the kind field is what a consumer branches on.
